plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with narrow silvery-green leaves and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers held above the foliage. It is a favorite of pollinators, especially bees, and is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields for essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name Lavandula likely comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing large rounded clusters of showy flowers above broad, glossy, toothed leaves. It thrives in partial shade and moist, rich soil and is a classic feature of cottage and coastal gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn, peaking in late June in temperate regions
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in Europe, the Azores, and the eastern and Pacific United States
plants.funFact: Flower color depends on soil pH and aluminum availability: acidic soils produce blue blooms, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with daisy-like flowers featuring drooping rosy-purple petals around a prominent spiky orange-brown central cone. It tolerates heat and drought and attracts bees, butterflies, and goldfinches.
plants.location: Native to the central and eastern United States prairies and open woodlands; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone. Indigenous peoples of the Great Plains used it medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: An evergreen shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, up to 30 cm across, with a central cluster of tiny flowers surrounded by silky pink bracts. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peaks in Southern Hemisphere late autumn to spring, with flowering often occurring around June in winter-rainfall areas
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and the national cricket team is nicknamed 'the Proteas' after it.
